title: Callvale after: web ACLs at the edge and Network Firewall for outbound traffic
claim: Web ACLs stop the flood, and Network Firewall checks the domains of outbound traffic.
alt: After: web ACLs from Firewall Manager policies on CloudFront and the load balancer. Outbound traffic passes the NAT gateway, then a firewall endpoint.

edges.say: The CloudFront web ACL blocks fast addresses, common attacks and sign-ins found against its stolen credential database.
The load balancer's web ACL comes from a second policy, because Firewall Manager needs separate Firewall Manager policies for each Region.
Outbound traffic passes the NAT gateway, then a Network Firewall endpoint.

notes: Brief 08 story pair, 2-deep.md#decision-record. Same cells as edge-protection-before; web ACLs fill B2, B3. Firewall Manager in an unnamed administrator account: a Global policy for CloudFront and a Regional policy for the load balancer. No Shield Advanced. Step facts in the Markdown: waf-atp-inspects-login-attempts, firewall-manager-waf-policy-global-for-cloudfront. Step 3 order (NAT gateway, then firewall endpoint) follows the Network Firewall guide pages asymmetric-routing and arch-igw-ngw (fix-08).
